name: Methane released to air (fossil) — CH4
co2e_basis: One kilogram of methane released is one kilogram of methane; the inventory's IPCC GWP set (fossil methane) converts it to CO2e
source: Mass of gas released; GWP from IPCC AR5 Table 8.7 / AR6 Table 7.15 as selected
source_version: Definition: the quantity entered is the mass of CH4

name: FK-5-1-12 (Novec 1230) released to air — FK-5-1-12
co2e_basis: One kilogram released is one kilogram of FK-5-1-12; GWP-100 from AR6 Table 7.SM.7 (0.114) or the AR5 Table 8.A.1 bound (<1, used as 1)
source: Mass of gas released; GWP from IPCC AR6 Table 7.SM.7 / AR5 Table 8.A.1
source_version: Definition: the quantity entered is the mass of agent discharged

name: Acetylene burned (cutting / welding) — CO2
co2e_basis: Complete combustion C2H2 + 2.5 O2 -> 2 CO2 + H2O: 2 x 44.009 / 26.038 = 3.3804 kg CO2 per kg acetylene (standard atomic weights). No published table gives this; it is the stoichiometry.

name: Hydrogen burned on site — CO2
co2e_basis: Hydrogen contains no carbon (2 H2 + O2 -> 2 H2O), so burning it releases no CO2. Emissions from producing grey hydrogen are upstream and belong in Scope 3 Category 1 or 3, not here.

name: R-717 (ammonia) refrigerant released — CO2e
co2e_basis: Ammonia (NH3) is not a greenhouse gas under the GHG Protocol or the Kyoto basket and has no IPCC GWP, so a leak adds 0 kg CO2e. Record it for safety, not for the inventory.
source_version: NH3 is outside the seven GHG Protocol gases

name: Commute on foot or by bicycle — CO2e
co2e_basis: No fuel or electricity is used, so the journey has 0 kg CO2e. Record it so the commuting survey is complete.

name: Emissions entered directly in tonnes of CO2e — CO2e
co2e_basis: The quantity entered is already tonnes of CO2e: 1 t = 1,000 kg CO2e. Attach the calculation that produced it as evidence.
source: Direct entry: your own calculated tCO2e

name: Incineration of industrial waste, no energy recovery — CO2
co2e_basis: Equation 5.2 with Table 5.2 defaults for industrial waste: carbon 50% of dry weight x fossil fraction 90% x oxidation 100% x 44/12 = 1.65 t CO2 per tonne of DRY waste
source: IPCC 2006 Guidelines, Volume 5 Chapter 5 (Incineration and Open Burning of Waste)
licence: IPCC Guidelines, free to use with attribution

name: Incineration of industrial waste, no energy recovery — N2O
co2e_basis: Table 5.6: 100 g N2O per tonne of industrial waste, all incineration types (IPCC states it on wet weight)
source: IPCC 2006 Guidelines, Volume 5 Chapter 5 (Incineration and Open Burning of Waste)
licence: IPCC Guidelines, free to use with attribution

name: Incineration of sewage sludge — CO2
co2e_basis: Table 5.2: the fossil carbon fraction of sewage sludge is 0%, so its CO2 is biogenic and outside the scopes
source: IPCC 2006 Guidelines, Volume 5 Chapter 5 (Incineration and Open Burning of Waste)
licence: IPCC Guidelines, free to use with attribution

name: Incineration of sewage sludge — N2O
co2e_basis: Table 5.6: 990 g N2O per tonne of sewage sludge on a dry-weight basis
source: IPCC 2006 Guidelines, Volume 5 Chapter 5 (Incineration and Open Burning of Waste)
licence: IPCC Guidelines, free to use with attribution

name: Hydrogen production, natural gas steam reforming — CO2
co2e_basis: Equation 3.45 (Tier 1b) with Table 3.30: 165 GJ natural gas per tonne H2 x 0.0153 t C per GJ x 44/12 = 9.2565 t CO2 per tonne of hydrogen, before any CO2 recovered
source: 2019 Refinement to the 2006 IPCC Guidelines, Volume 3 Chapter 3 (Chemical Industry), section 3.11
licence: IPCC Guidelines, free to use with attribution

name: Biochar from wood, pyrolysis 450-600 C, carbon stored after 100 years — CO2 removed
co2e_basis: Equation 4Ap.1: organic carbon 0.77 t C per tonne dry biochar (Table 4Ap.1, wood, pyrolysis) x 0.80 remaining after 100 years (Table 4Ap.2, 450-600 C) x 44/12 = 2.2587 t CO2 removed per tonne. Reported separately, never netted off.
source: 2019 Refinement to the 2006 IPCC Guidelines, Volume 4 Chapter 2 Appendix 4 (Biochar)
licence: IPCC Guidelines, free to use with attribution

name: Energy balance line (no emissions counted) — CO2e
co2e_basis: Scope 2 Guidance section 5.4: power a company makes and uses itself, and power it exports, add no Scope 2 emissions. Recorded for the energy balance only.

name: Sold product reused at end of life — CO2e
category_path: End of life / derived by definition
co2e_basis: A product that is reused is not treated or disposed of, so it adds no end-of-life emissions to the company that sold it.
source: Derived: definition (GHG Protocol Scope 3 Standard, Category 12)
